texts.facts: This writ Petition is filed by the petitioner seeking direction to the respondent not to forcibly evict the petitioner without providing a suitable place to relocate his bunk shop and also seeking direction to the respondent to formulate a scheme in line with the National Policy on Urban Street Vendors, 2009 for rehabilitation of the petitioner in case he is evicted from the present place for some reasons and to implement the scheme. 2. Material facts for the disposal of the writ petition are as follows:- Petitioner is a street vendor and as a means of livelihood for the family, petitioner is running a small bunk near Lissie hospital buildings by the side of the public road since 1990, where he is vending tea, coffee, snacks and thereby eking out a livelihood for himself and his family. According to the petitioner, the licencing authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act has issued Ext.P2 Registration Certificate to the petitioner valid till 30.03.2018 for running a coffee shop. While so, during October 2013, officials of Corporation of Cochin came to the bunk and demanded the petitioner to vacate the bunk forthwith and threatened that if the petitioner does not vacate immediately they will be forced to forcibly evict the petitioner. According to the petitioner, he is entitled to the benefits of National Policy on Street Vendors, 2009 and it is thus seeking appropriate directions, this writ petition is filed. 3. A counter affidavit is filed by the respondent basically contenting that as per the records available with the Corporation, bunk No.170 in question is in the name of one M.P.Muhammed. As to how petitioner has come in occupation of the bunk is not stated by him. According to the respondent the person to whom the bunk was allotted is no more and the occupation of the petitioner is unauthorized. That apart it is contented that, the bunk shop causes serious hindrances to the traffic. The Lissie hospital residence association have filed certain complaints before the respondent requesting to remove the unauthorised bunks. The residence association filed a petition before the Shamsu. C vs Corporation Of Cochin on 24 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37218977/ 3 Ombudsman for local self government institutions in which Corporation was a respondent, evident from Ext.R1 complaint. The Ombudsman conducted an enquiry on the complaint which was taken on file and notices were issued, evident from Ext.R2. Subsequently after considering the entire issues Ext.R3 order is issued calling upon the Corporation to give 15 days notice to the bunk owners and report back the course of action being taken by the Corporation to the Ombudsman. On the basis of the enquiry, thereafter as per an order dated 16.9.2010 Ombudsman has passed an order directing the Corporation to evict unauthorised bunk shops evident from Ext.R4. But when steps were initiated by the Corporation to remove the unauthorised bunk shops various persons filed writ petition before this Court against the eviction of the bunk shops, consequent to which various interim orders were passed by this Court. However, repeated complaints were made by the local public, questioning the lethargy on the part of the Corporation from initiating action against the unauthorised bunks. That apart it is stated that the bunk of the petitioner is situated on the side of the very narrow road leading to the railway line from the front side of the Lissie Hospital road. On the one side of the road two wheelers are being parked and the bunk is protruding to the road it causes great difficulties and inconveniences even to the pedestrians. Various other contentions are raised in order to justify the action initiated by the Corporation to remove the bunk shop. I had also advantage of hearing the Lissie Hospital Road Residents Association which got impleaded by filing I.A. No.5121/2017.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner is conducting the shop in accordance with law and Ext.P2 Registration Certificate issued by the Food Safety Authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is a clear testimony to establish that petitioner is operating the bunk shop in accordance with law. On a perusal of Ext.P2 licence of the petitioner was renewed from 01.04.2012 to 31.03.2013 and from 31.03.2013 to 30.03.2018. The address of the business premises is shown as Door No.3. According to the petitioner, licence is issued against the bunk shop in question. 6. However, learned counsel appearing for the respondents submitted that Ext.P2 licence is issued to a different shop and the bunk shop occupied by the petitioner is having No.170 provided by the Corporation of Cochin and the same is not having any licence issued by the Food Safety Authority. Moreover, it is contented that the said bunk shop was originally given to one M.P.Muhammed, who is no more and therefore petitioner is an unauthorised occupant of the bunk shop. If the petitioner is entitled as per the provisions of the Act to be included as a street vendor then petitioner is entitled to get protection as per Section 3(3) of the said Act, till such time the petitioner is relocated. The bunk was allotted to another person on whose death the permission granted had come to Shamsu.
